text: Let's begin Lesson 6.
In this lecture, we will learn how to use our calendar to structure our day.

In this lesson, we will learn, first, what trying to run your day from memory or relying only on your routines leads to; second of all, how to use our calendar to give our day a structure; and third of all, using your morning routine or routines in general to schedule your
first of all, we will have to talk about what happens when you're trying to run your day from memory or relying only on routines.
The first thing which happens is that there is a lot of randomness.
You start to do stuff and then you switch, and then you start to do that again and then you switch.
It's a lot of randomness: you start something, you leave it, then you start something else, and you probably leave that as well, and then you'll find out that the day is over.
The second thing which happens is that
lack of time awareness: hours pass without knowing.
You don't have the awareness of time; you just go on with your day and your hours just pass, and when you look at your day, you haven't really done anything.
The third thing is inconsistency: you will not be really consistent in doing the right stuff every single day.
And again, this is linked to randomness, where you're doing random stuff most of the
time.
You are just doing random stuff, and when you're doing random stuff, that just shows that you will not really be consistent in doing the right stuff or the important stuff which you have to do.
The fourth thing is you will skip tasks.
For example, let's say today you start to do immediately your red task, or your most important task for the day, but the thing happens: while you are working,
suddenly an idea pops up and you can't get rid of the ideas in your mind.
And so, when you don't really have a time period or scheduled time where you will only focus on this thing, the idea will pull you.
You, most likely, a lot of times are going to go and try to do that idea.
So, you were doing something important, but you don't really have the time estimate in your mind; you were just kind of saying, "I have all my day,"
which is a good thing.
But what is happening is that you're getting rid of the most important tasks, which you would feel so much more pleasure by doing, and it will move you closer to the big goal that you have.
And the fifth thing, and the final one, is that you waste energy.
So, one thing which we kind of notice in here is that, all of this time, we're just kind of mostly wasting our energy.
You're kind of doing random stuff.
You don't really have that focus on just doing the most important stuff.

You don't really have the time estimate of what it will take you to do this, so you just go on with your day knowing that you have to complete the important task, or the tasks in general, but you're just getting pulled away to other, different stuff, and you're just not focused on the most important one.
And that's why I'm saying that you will just waste energy most of the
time.
And as we said in the last lecture, a routine can start our day, but it can't organize our entire life.
Or at least, that is how it was for me when I tried organizing my full life or my whole day only using routines—it just did not work at all.
All of these steps which I have mentioned, they were starting to appear throughout my day.
And so, for that, we will be using a calendar to give our day a structure.
We will be just using
two simple steps.
First of all, we will be using our morning or night routines, where we plan our day, where we schedule our day.
We will just take 5 to 10 minutes maximum to schedule our day.
And again, we can do this at night, but we can also do it in the morning.
I personally do it in the morning, as I said in the previous lecture, where in my morning routine, I have my scheduling, and you can do that as well within
the routine, where you schedule your tasks—the things which you have to do tomorrow or, if it's in the morning, the things which you have to do today.
So, what I need you to do is to implement this into your routine (morning, night, or even evening) where there's a time period in your mind.
You don't have to schedule it there, but just as a routine where how much time it takes doesn't matter, but inside there, there is scheduling.
While you are scheduling, what we will do is, of course, we will use the daily tasks—the red, yellow, and blue from the Kanban board which we have.
So, from the tasks which we have broken down to what we are going to do tomorrow or today, we will use them to schedule on our calendar.
We will block times in our calendar to completing those goals.
So, by doing this, our calendar becomes a daily
plan of exactly what to do next.

And how we do this is that we, first of all, open our Kanban board—the daily tasks which are in our Kanban board, the stuff which we have to do today or tomorrow—and then, for example, let's say it's the morning.
You go into your Kanban board, you see the tasks which you have to do today.
If not—so, if you haven't put the labels red, yellow, and blue, red being the most important,
yellow important, and blue optional—you can go ahead and do that.

But most likely, if you have just one goal, you don't have to really put anything because it's as simple as this: it's mostly red, which is like "must do." But if there are a lot of tasks, you can definitely label them: what is the most important, and then something which is important, but then the third one which is optional.
And then the third thing to do is to create
your time blocks for each task.

For red tasks, you should put them first, and then yellow after red tasks, and then blue, of course, the optional ones, if you can see that there is time in your day in which you can complete them and you want to do them.
You can definitely do that.
And by doing this, we give our day a structure and we remove decision-making.

board.

do it today.

tasks divided with labels, so we can know which one we should complete and the ones which would be nice to complete.

you have throughout your day.

So you can just schedule all of these important
tasks which you have before work or after work.
So, it's up to you in your case what you need to do, but the main point of this was so you have control over your time, you have control over your tasks fully.

And the thing to note is that, when you are especially starting to schedule your stuff in the calendar in the beginning, you are going to make some time errors, especially when you are starting something
new, which you don't really have experience of.
You will definitely make time errors, where you say that this will take 30 minutes, you schedule it like that, but that takes an hour.
Or the other way around, where you schedule this for one hour, but this only took 30 minutes.
And for that, you can definitely use tools or just a note to just see how much time it has taken you to do this.
And this is a process where, after some time, you will know how much time it will take to do a certain
task, and then you just schedule them the way you want.
And again, over time, you will just become more of an expert; your calendar is just the beginning when you will get used to doing it, but the important stuff is that you do your work.
You have now full control over your time, and throughout the day you don't have to worry about what to do because you have it in your calendar—you have everything on your calendar.
So now you can definitely go ahead and grab your

tasks which you have to do today or tomorrow, and go ahead and schedule them in the calendar which you choose to use—of course, preferably being a digital one, because you have it with you everywhere you go, and it will not really get cleared, and you can edit it throughout the day.

And, for example, if you're watching this at night or in the evening, you can leave to do this task tomorrow morning; but also, you can leave it to do it at night, maybe related to your night routine or evening
routine.

Just take 5 to 10 minutes, see what you're going to do tomorrow, and of course to know, for example, when you will wake up; and basing it on your logic, at what time you're going to finish your morning routine and then start your tasks.

But for me, again, I do it in the morning, so there are times which I may wake up a little bit later than I expected, and so I just know that I will just do my morning routine, and after my morning routine the scheduling is done because it's a part of it, and then I don't have to worry
about what I will do next and to leave it to randomness.
And that is literally it—now you will have time control over your life and your goals and your time.
